https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/production-ready-enterprise-ai-agent-coding-harness-steve-nouri-1x92c?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BLsRs%2BpchTEqwNzxKca%2FDYg%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=19itZNJqmGyso1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mt2x8nda~rg-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mt2x8nda-rg
  
Most projects hit the same wall: The demo works. Production doesn’t. A team picks a use case, spends a few weeks building a POC, gets strong accuracy, decent latency and acceptable cost. Everyone gets excited. Then security, compliance and operations enter the room. Can we reconstruct every action the agent took? What data did it access? Under whose authorization? Can sensitive data stay inside the customer environment? Where does a human approve a high-risk decision? How do we know performance hasn’t drifted six months from now? These are architecture questions. If the system wasn’t designed around them, teams usually start bolting controls onto the POC. That is where things get brittle. Anthropic’s Christopher Lovejoy and Anterior’s Saul Marquez recently shared a useful architecture pattern from deploying agents in healthcare. The same ideas transfer well to finance, defense, government and other regulated environments. 1. Make every agent action replayable A normal developer log is not enough. For an enterprise agent, you want an immutable event log containing the actions taken, data accessed and authorization used. Think event sourcing: one append-only record across the system. The useful side effect is that you can reconstruct the state of the system at any point in time. That helps with compliance, debugging and later evaluation. Practical rule: if an important agent decision gets challenged three months later, your architecture should let you replay exactly what happened. 2. Keep sensitive data separate from orchestration The event stream should record what happened. The underlying sensitive data can live separately in immutable object storage, with the event log holding references to it. That separation matters. Developers can inspect the agent’s path without automatically getting access to the underlying healthcare, financial or customer data. Access can be granted at the point of use using scoped tokens and zero-trust controls. This is increasingly important for enterprise agents because the blast radius changes when a model can both read private data and take actions. 3. Design human escalation into the agent runtime Human-in-the-loop often gets implemented as an exception handler: If confidence < 80%, send this to someone. Real workflows are messier. Escalation may depend on uncertainty, policy, transaction size, clinical

77795.subject: Ramp is building the CFO for AI Agents 📊🤖; Stripe’s leaked investor letter says the Singularity started January …
77795.body:
View this post on the web at https://linas.substack.com/p/fintechpulse1116

Hey Everyone,
Good morning & happy Friday! Today, we’re diving into Ramp's launch of Router.com to see why the product they shipped alongside it, not the router LLM itself, is the bigger move here (the Stripe vs Ramp routing war, how USDC agent wallets turn AI agents into controlled corporate spenders, who wins between developers and CFOs + bonus deep dives into How to Build an Agentic OS with Claude Fable 5 [ https://substack.com/redirect/460e1710-37f4-4322-ac9b-4945d60afd87?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] & The AI Monopoly Playbook [ https://substack.com/redirect/b8b76725-24bc-4aff-b51b-0efa4d8684cc?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] inside), and Stripe's leaked investor letter to see why Patrick Collison told his investors the singularity started on January 1st and what that means for the $7B OpenRouter deal (Stripe's H1 2026 financials, the "two currencies" thesis that reframes the entire acquisition, plus the product stack that turns tokens into a payment rail + bonus deep dive into The Ultimate Guide to Qwen3.8-27B [ https://substack.com/redirect/5f03e78c-4d0c-4418-8434-22281c7d5473?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] inside). So let’s jump straight into the finnovative stuff 🌶️
Ramp is building the CFO for AI Agents 📊🤖
The news 🗞️ When we first covered Ramp Router [ https://substack.com/redirect/bc13d98a-fbf7-4cfd-813c-1d522d21a13a?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] on July 22, we clearly said it is not a product but rather a wedge into AI spend management. A month later, the picture is even bigger than we thought.
On Wednesday, Ramp launched Router.com, an AI model routing service built on 3 years of internal production use. Hours earlier, Stripe had officially confirmed its $7.5B acquisition of OpenRouter [ https://substack.com/redirect/83a63b66-0f63-49d1-b8df-9b2c21b1ef23?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], the developer-favorite model marketplace, at nearly 6x the valuation it held just three months prior.
These two companies are not strangers. Stripe co-led Ramp’s 2021 Series B at a $1.6B valuation and still provides card-issuing and stablecoin infrastructure that Ramp relies on today.
Now they want the same layer: the routing decision that determines which AI model gets paid per request. And that’s before you account for what Ramp shipped alongside the router. That second product may actually matter more than the router itself...

77664.subject: Online check-in for a smooth take-off. ATTENTION! Don’t forget – it opens 24 hours before departure. (Y9SB5U)

Hello, Oleh Novosadov!

Your adventure is just around the corner – you’ll soon be boarding your Ryanair flight! There’s just one small step left to ensure a smooth start: online check-in.

It’s easy – do it via the Ryanair app. This way, you avoid unnecessary fees at the airport..

How to do it? Here’s a quick guide:

You will need:
- Booking code: Y9SB5U
- Booking email: novosadov@boarding.sk (it may differ from your personal email address)

If you’re using the Ryanair mobile app, you can check in directly there – it’s fast, convenient and eco-friendly.

When is check-in available?
- From 24 to 2 hours before departure
- If you’ve purchased seats, you can check in as early as 60 days before your flight

Download your boarding passes.

Save them in the app – you’ll need them when going through airport security. Before your trip, make sure your BOARDING PASSES (tickets) are in ELECTRONIC FORM. Download them to your phone.

You’ll find a full step-by-step guide with screenshots in our manual for checking in online via the Ryanair app.

ATTENTION! If you leave the check-in until the airport, it may cost you up to €55.
